children: Gorilla Gold Mines
has agreed to acquire the Cosmos project from IGO Limited
, adding a Western Australian exploration district and nickel-processing infrastructure to its gold portfolio.
The binding transaction will give Gorilla ownership of the project, with completion of the deal conditional on shareholder approval and agreements governing lithium rights retained by IGO.
The acquisition includes a refurbished nickel concentrator with capacity of 1.1 million tonnes per annum, together with tailings facilities, an aerodrome, water systems, and accommodation.

Gorilla estimates the replacement value of the existing infrastructure at more than $300 million, and conversion to gold processing remains an option subject to exploration success, engineering, and technical assessment, with the existing flotation circuit potentially retained for nickel and copper.
The company has subsequently received firm commitments for a $60m placement to finance drilling and integration, with resources investor Tembo Capital committing half the proceeds.
Cosmos Reshapes Gold Portfolio
Under the share purchase agreement, Gorilla will acquire all shares in IGO Cosmos Pty Ltd, which owns the Cosmos project approximately 30 kilometres north of Leinster, adjoining Bellevue Gold's
operation.
IGO will receive approximately 238.3 million Gorilla shares based on the placement structure, giving it a 19.9% stake subject to a 12-month voluntary escrow.

The vendor will also receive two tranches of 32.5 million performance rights linked to Cosmos gold-resource thresholds or Gorilla share-price milestones, while keeping exclusive lithium rights under a separate agreement.

The required minimum $30m financing condition will be satisfied once the first placement tranche settles, but third-party lithium consents and approval for consideration securities are still outstanding.
Historical Gold Systems

Cosmos has recorded historical gold production of approximately 120,744 ounces at an average grade of 6.0 grams per tonne, although those production records are not current mineral resource or ore reserve estimates.
Limited systematic gold exploration followed the conclusion of mining by Ramelius Resources
in 2016, leaving several systems open along strike and at depth.
At Main Road, historical unmined intersections include 20m at 40.3g/t gold from 18m and 18m at 35.8g/t from 25m, while the Jones Creek system extends for more than 5km.
Gorilla has identified Main Road, Jones Creek, and Orleans for systematic follow-up, with historical drilling and production not guaranteeing future discoveries or commercial outcomes.

Cosmos lies 68km by sealed road from Gorilla’s Vivien Project and near its North Kalgoorlie Hub, which together hold an existing mineral resource base of approximately 1.5 million ounces at 3.8g/t gold.
Cornerstone Placement
The two-tranche placement comprises about 226.4 million new shares at 26.5 cents each, matching the previous closing price and representing a 6% premium to the 10-day volume-weighted average price.
Tembo will subscribe for $30m, with the balance supported by institutional investors, while directors have committed $2.4m subject to shareholder approval.
Including the entire placement and existing cash, Gorilla forecasts pro-forma cash of $69.5m with no debt before transaction and placement costs, assuming completion of both tranches.
Its proposed allocation includes $25m for Cosmos exploration, $12.5m for the North Kalgoorlie Hub, and $10m for Vivien, alongside discretionary growth funding and corporate costs.
Leadership Change
The expansion coincides with Simon Lawson moving from non-executive director to executive chair, bringing Cosmos experience and a mandate to develop Gorilla’s exploration-led growth strategy.
Mr Lawson previously served as managing director and executive chair of Spartan Resources before its acquisition by Ramelius in 2025, and also worked as a geologist at Cosmos earlier in his career.
He replaces Dean Hely as chair, with Mr Hely remaining a non-executive director and Charles Hughes continuing as chief executive officer.

Mr Lawson will invest $1m through the placement and has been offered 24 million performance rights, subject to shareholder approval, with vesting tied to resource growth or defined share-price hurdles.

title: Gorilla Gold Mines to Acquire Cosmos Gold Project Backed By $60m Raising
